title: The ball that snitched on Ronaldo
script: Ronaldo celebrated. But did he touch it? The ball carried evidence. Inside, a suspension system stabilises an inertial measurement unit, or IMU. An accelerometer measures changes in motion. A gyroscope measures how fast the ball rotates. It samples five hundred times a second. That's one reading every two milliseconds, not a verdict every two milliseconds. A touch can produce a sudden change in the signal. Adidas said Ronaldo's attempted header produced no measurable external force. The goal went to Bruno Fernandes. For offside checks, software combines ball timing with camera-tracked player positions. Video officials validate the suggested kick point and offside line. The sensor helps establish when. Officials interpret the play. Follow TechWhoKnows for the tech behind the moment.
